subject: Request: regional support-hour exceptions & branding footnote for CloudBridge listing
messages:
From: Hannah Price <hannah.price@cloudbridge.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2029-12-01T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Marketplace listing: support hours & branding question

Hi Ben / Marissa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. The CloudBridge product team is excited to move into marketplace listing prep for AWS and Azure. Two quick asks from our side before we hand this off to our partner ops teams: 

1) Support hours: our current support commitment to enterprise customers is "business hours" PST (M–F 09:00–17:00), but several of our co-sell prospects in APAC require 24x7 incident intake or an explicit escalation footnote. Can you confirm whether Redwood has a standard approach for requesting an "hourly coverage exception" or footnote on marketplace listings?

2) Branding / claims: Audit raised two flagged claims in our listing copy ("real-time inference at scale" and an implication of SLAs). Marketplace teams often want a short footnote or modified phrasing. Can your team propose a neutral footnote that satisfies AWS/Azure reviewers while preserving marketing intent?

I've attached a short product doc and the draft listing text. If possible, we need guidance by end of week because the listing intake window opens on Monday for the co-sell batch.

Attachments: CloudBridge_Product_Doc.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

—Hannah
Hannah Price
Head of GTM Partnerships | CloudBridge
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Price <hannah.price@cloudbridge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-12-01T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing: support hours & branding question

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear asks and the doc. Quick responses and next steps below.

1) Support hours / hourly coverage exception: short answer — yes, we can request an exception or a footnote on the marketplace listing that calls out regional support routing and expected response windows. It is handled case-by-case by marketplace ops (AWS/Azure). The exception request should include:
  - Exact regional hours you want to publish (e.g., 09:00–18:00 AEDT for APAC)
  - Whether you will provide 24x7 on-call for severity-1 incidents (and how those incidents are triaged)
  - Escalation contact (email + phone/pager if any) and expected initial response SLA (e.g., 1 hour)

I've attached a template schedule (support_schedule_matrix.xlsx) for you to fill out; that helps speed AWS/Azure reviewers. If you want Redwood to request the exception on your behalf, we'll need a short authorization email from CloudBridge and the filled matrix.

2) Branding / claims wording: marketplace reviewers dislike absolute claims ("real-time") unless you include a qualifying timeframe or a measured benchmark. Proposed short footnote we typically use: "Claim qualified: Real-time as defined by sub-second median tail latency under our listed instance types; see performance profile for details." That phrasing preserves the claim but points reviewers to a performance profile page rather than a blanket SLA.

Next steps: Hannah, can you fill the attached matrix and return by EOD Thursday? Marissa / Kim — if you're available I propose we prepare: (a) authorization email for Redwood to act as a submitter, (b) the proposed footnote copy for each marketplace (AWS, Azure, GCP), and (c) an evidence bundle (SOC2 snapshot + performance profile + filled matrix).

Attaching: support_schedule_matrix.xlsx

If helpful, I can draft the authorization email and the footnote variants for review.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-12-02T11:38:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Marketplace listing: support hours & branding question — internal draft

Kim / Jonas — forwarding Hannah's note with my responses. Keeping this internal: below is a proposed package to send to AWS/Azure listing reviewers. Please review and flag anything that would block co-sell enablement.

PROPOSED PACKAGE (for partner ops intake):
- Authorization: one-line from CloudBridge authorizing Redwood to submit and request exceptions on their behalf.
- Support schedule: filled matrix (APAC specifics highlighted).
- Evidence: SOC2 snapshot (most recent), summary of monitoring/alerting, and a compact performance profile (median & p95 under typical instance types).
- Listing footnote variants (choose one per marketplace):
  * Neutral: "Claim qualified: For details on observed latencies and test configuration, see our published performance profile."
  * Stronger (if needed): "Claim qualified: Sub-second median latency observed in evaluated configs; actual latency varies by instance size and input length."

I attached a draft copy for the listing that strips absolute SLA language — please see proposed_listing_copy.txt. If you're OK, I'll (a) send the draft footnote to CloudBridge for quick approval, and (b) submit the intake with AWS/Azure ops next week.

Notes: AWS tends to push back on phone-based escalation being published on the listing; they prefer email + escalated ticketing IRT. Azure sometimes allows a short footnote around regional hours. GCP has been strict on any claim that looks like a promise of uptime without a formal SLA. Recommend we mark GCP as "review-only" for now and pursue AWS/Azure first for co-sell batch.

—Ben

[Attachment: proposed_listing_copy.txt]
From: Hannah Price <hannah.price@cloudbridge.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-12-03T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing: support hours & branding question

Thanks Ben — this is super helpful. I've attached the completed support matrix and SOC2 snapshot. CloudBridge approves Redwood to submit on our behalf (see short authorization below).

Authorization: "CloudBridge authorizes Redwood Inference to submit listing materials and request support-hour/footnote exceptions for the CloudBridge listing in AWS and Azure marketplaces."

We prefer the Neutral footnote variant you proposed for AWS; for Azure we can try the stronger variant if the intake reviewer asks for more specificity. We do not want to publish phone numbers on the listing; email + a designated on-call alias are fine.

Next steps from our side:
- Confirm you have what you need to submit Monday morning.
- If you submit on CloudBridge's behalf, please share the intake ticket ID and any reviewer notes.

Attachments: support_schedule_matrix.xlsx, SOC2_snapshot.pdf

Appreciate the fast turnaround — excited to get this into the co-sell batch.

—Hannah
Hannah Price
Head of GTM Partnerships | CloudBridge
